Learning class-dependent graph combinations

300 conversations · nine score layers · 14 classes · both window sizes · no new Jev calls.

The learned coefficients combine score-layer adjacencies before the Laplacians are computed. Each class has its own nine nonnegative weights summing to one. Missing layers are excluded and the remaining weights are renormalized separately for each edge.

Weights were selected by three inner task-group folds, entirely within each outer training fold. The search compared 65 fixed mixtures, penalizing deviation from equal weights. The classifier, feature definitions and outer test splits stayed unchanged. The full-data weight tables are refitted models; they did not produce the held-out scores below.

What the numbers mean

AP is average precision across the 14 reference labels, not accuracy. F1 uses the existing fixed 0.5 threshold. The paired intervals resample task groups from saved held-out predictions and do not include retraining uncertainty.

This follow-up is exploratory because the outer test sets had already been inspected. The search is finite rather than a continuous optimum. Annotation, missing-context, unconfirmed-interaction and graph-projection limitations from the previous experiment remain.

31 unit tests passed. Both audits verified all inner selections and reconstructed every outer prediction. Selected graph features were additionally recomputed with the scalar Laplacian implementation on a fixed 30-conversation sample.
